title: Antim ardas: for him, or for us?
hook: the bhog and final Ardas close the mourning
carry: the final prayer asks rest for them, strength for us
tomorrow: the mourning is officially over. why is Bebe still crying?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a reading after death: read for them, every page, at whatever speed you have. Today the last page is read.

The gurdwara hall is fuller than Simran expected: truckers in clean shirts, Gurnam flown in from far away, Maya and her mom near the back. The granthi reads the closing pages of the Granth. That's the bhog, the completion. Then the whole sangat stands for the antim ardas, the final prayer. On the drive home, an aunty says, so beautiful, the ardas for Baba's soul. Harjit, eyes on the road, says quietly, it's for us, really. Simran, in the back seat, can't tell which of them is right.
screen: `THE CLOSING PAGES: BHOG.` → `EVERYONE STANDS.` → `FOR BABA'S SOUL, OR FOR US?`

segments.voice: Both views live inside the Sikh community, so let each speak. First, the aunty. The final prayer is for him. In the Ardas, the sangat asks Waheguru to give the one who has gone a place at the Guru's feet. A community stands together and asks, out loud, on behalf of someone who can no longer ask for himself. That's love with somewhere to go. Now Harjit. The final prayer is for us. Guru Nanak, in Asa ki Vaar on Ang 472, mocks a custom of feeding others in the ancestors' name: in paraphrase, if a thief robs a house and gives the goods in his ancestors' name, the goods are recognized in the next world, and he makes his ancestors thieves. What a person did travels with them; nobody can send it on afterward. So the prayer is for the living: strength to accept the Will, and to carry on well. And here's the thing worth telling a friend tonight: in the Ardas Simran heard, both requests were there. Rest at the Guru's feet for Baba. For the family, the strength to accept the Will. The aunty and Harjit each heard half of it.
screen: `ONE VIEW: IT'S FOR HIM.` · `ANOTHER VIEW: IT'S FOR US.` · `ANG 472: DEEDS CAN'T BE SENT ON.` · `BOTH, IN ONE ARDAS.` · then, large: `THE FINAL PRAYER.`

segments.voice: If you pray, stand or sit straight with your palms together, the way the sangat stands for Ardas, and hold in mind someone who has died. If not, keep the posture and simply remember them: a face, a laugh, one thing they used to say.
Antim ardas: the final prayer, said standing when the complete reading reaches its bhog, closing the formal mourning.
Keep this: the final prayer asks rest for them, strength for us, in one breath. That's it for today.

howItsDone: When the reading begun after a death reaches its bhog, the sangat stands for the antim ardas, asking peace for the departed and strength for the family to accept the Will; karah prashad and langar follow.

chat.says: aunty said the ardas was 'for baba's soul.' dad said 'it's for us.' who's right
options: both. the Ardas asked rest for Baba and strength for the family to accept.
aunty; the prayer's only job is to get Baba's soul to a good place.
dad; Sikhs don't pray for the dead at all, only for the living.
chat.meaning: The final prayer holds both: a place at the Guru's feet for the one who has gone, and strength for the living to accept the Will.

tie.story: In the Ardas at the bhog, the sangat asked a place at the Guru's feet for Baba and strength for his family to accept the Will.
